Light Blue Eau Intense Pour Homme by Dolce&Gabbana is a Woody Aquatic fragrance for men. Light Blue Eau Intense Pour Homme was launched in 2017. The nose behind this fragrance is Alberto Morillas. Top notes are Grapefruit and Mandarin Orange; middle notes are Sea water and Juniper; base notes are Musk and Amberwood.

Light Blue Pour Homme Eau Intense is developed by Alberto Morillas. The fragrance opens with citrusy notes of mandarin and frozen grapefruit. The heart of juniper and a salty marine accord is wrapped up by the base of amber wood and musk.It is available as a 50, 100 and 200 ml Eau de Parfum.

AStrachn 11/19/25 02:53

Dolce & Gabbana Light Blue Pour Homme Intense is the perfect summer scent, capturing those bright, vibrant days. It's clean, intensely fresh, and boasts great longevity. The opening I get grapefruit, juniper, aquatic notes that boost invigorating freshness. It dries into a lightly sweet amberwood where I still get a flicker of juniper from time to time. I adore this scent.

This a true compliment-getter and a must-have for warm weather, although this can be used most of the year. A confident, high-performance upgrade to the classic I used since I was a kid. You can dress Light Blue Intense up or down with ease. You can go heavy without being too potent when around people. It was my main fragrance for the longest time.

Sillage is within arms reach, but a whispy fly by in the office will get you subtly noticed. As I said before, longevity is pretty much 8+ hours. I only re-apply during the day to smell the opening again. I highly recommend, especially since this iteration might be discontinued.

Eau de GT 11/05/25 17:33

The Beach Fragrance.
This is probably one of, if not the, greatest beach fragrances ever made.

You’re not supposed to wear fragrance to the beach, it usually comes off as tacky or socially clueless.
But I made the perfect mistake:
I sprayed this on my arm in a store to test it before heading to the beach for the day.
I jumped into the ocean, swam, relaxed, and this thing held strong even after sunset.

Now I understand why D&G markets this with men walking up from the sea.
It blends perfectly with salt water, making you smell fresh and oceanic. Like, really fresh-salty.
You literally smell like a sexy ocean.

People throw around the word oceanic for all kinds of scents, usually by people who’ve probably never been to the sea.
The ocean smells like salt, seaweed, and marine organisms.

Outside of the ocean, it opens sharp, tangy, and fresh, then quickly dries down to a sweet, clean, fabric softener-type scent.
Very boring.
But in ocean water, this is truly unique, sexy, and unforgettable.

I test Light Blue Eau Intense Pour Homme from Dolce & Gabbana in few diffrent moments, just to see how it behave.

FishJackl 09/24/25 00:27

Before I give my review let me clarify that this is my own experience with this fragrance and everyone's experience will vary.

This fragrance is good, but I feel like it could've been better and is missing a little something. The opening is nice to me although others didn't find it as appealing as it was to me, the opening is very citrusy with some small hits of mandarine orange, but to be I smell the rind or skin of the orange, and not get any fruityness from it. After about 15-30 minutes you start to pick up on more notes like the sea water and the juniper starts to come in as well, in my opinion I feel that the juniper doesn't fit to well I'm this fragrance as it makes it a bit herbaceous and like herby green which doesn't fit the citrus and sea water, I would've preferred something else like fig to make it smell cleaner. After about an hour or two the juniper starts to fade a little more and that's when this fragrance starts to smell very addictive to me. The dry down is fine but it honestly smells pretty woody which doesn't suit this fragrance too well but it's alright. I'm not sure if this is my bottle or just my skin chemistry but the performance is honestly not great for me, it lasts about 6 hours before it almost completely disappears and after the 6 hour mark the fragrance low-key fades and is gone, I wouldn't expect it to last you an entire school day with good performance so you might have to touch up. The silliage is very okay projection is fine for the first two and a half hours about arms length then it after 4 hours it becomes a skin scent. I'm kinda disappointed by the performance but I don't mind touching up and it's farly inexpensive for a designer fragrance but I expected a lot better performance from an EDP. Overall it smells very refreshing and smells like a summer day on the beach, but for me at least the performance marks a few points for me.

UltraGroyper 09/04/25 02:15

PREFACE

Ive been wearing this fragrance for a few days now and I must say this has easily become my #1 blue fragrance. This is exactly what my I'm looking for in a blue fragrance so there may be bias in my review.

SCENT PROFILE

if your anything like me I hate snobnose complicated fragrance explanations so here's a simple one for those who appreciate it:

top notes:
- Lemon zest with a oceanic twist. Imagine if lemons grew in the ocean.
- Oceanic salt.
- Airiness / musk
- Soap

Dry down:
- Lemon Zest, slightly fainter.
- Ocean salt, but now with ocean sugar!
- airiness / musk more prevalant
- soap basically the same.

PERFORMANCE:

This is a solid performer. 5 sprays gives me 3 - 5 hours of a solid 2 foot projection, at the 5 hour mark it becomes more intimate with a half a foot projection roughly, then becomes a skin scent at the 7 to 8 hour mark. Granted, the times I tested this were hotter, low to mid 80s so you might get better performance in cooler weather.

THOUGHTS:

This is the perfect blue fragrance, period. I will 100% be buying more when I run out. With that out of the way, this is a deliciously aquatic masculine fresh fragrance. It is unique enough to be a signature scent however I personally wouldn't go that far. It's very reasonably priced especially if your purchasing from a discounter, which I got mine for 80$

Overall for blue fragrance, although I am not one to give perfect scores, since this fragrance embodies everything I want, something cheap, aquatic, perfect for multiple occaaions, travel size, a little niche but appealing, this is a 10/10 fragrance.

On a tester strip, Light Blue Eau Intense is exactly what you'd hope for: a blast of salty, aquatic grapefruit that feels perfectly suited for a sweltering Florida day. I went in expecting to love this, given its legendary status as a summer staple.

Unfortunately, this is a prime example of why you must test fragrances on your own skin. The moment this touches my body, the story changes completely. That bright, appealing citrus vanishes and is replaced by an incredibly pungent, almost sour accord that, for me, comes across as the dreaded "wet dog" smell. It's a jarring and unpleasant opening that completely ruins the experience.

After about an hour, that initial sharpness thankfully fades. The dry down becomes a very subtle, quiet skin scent. While it's tolerable at this stage, it's also completely unremarkable and lacks any of the character promised by its reputation. There's nothing impressive or noteworthy left, just a faint whisper of what might have been.

I'm left feeling confused by this fragrance. I understand its mass appeal on paper, but my own skin chemistry makes it an impossible wear for me personally. This is a mandatory skin test—do not blind buy this one, no matter how good it sounds.

dream//housecc 06/29/25 14:13

Dolce & Gabbana Light Blue Eau Intense

This has slowly become the go-to summer staple of fresh aquatics. It is one of those flankers that just continue to give the OG its street credit. The name is fitting; it is the intense version of the original.

Granted you add in the saltiness of the sea water notes, and amberwood. This is still light blue. Is it redundant to have both? No. In my opinion, the OG is a tad bit more versatile and one you can dress up or dress down. The intense is versatile but it's more suit for the spring and summer white t-shirt and shorts. (Now you want to rock this one in a two-piece suit, or tux? Have at it.) You can wear what you paid for when you want to. These are just opinions that we make here.

Now to the performance. Longevity on the intense is great definitely bat's way above its class. Looking at 8 to 9 hours. Projection is also solid for about 2 hours. For a summer freshie, and aquatic at that this certainly is in that beast mode territory.

Now this is just my opinion. If you have a small collection and plan to keep to just what works. I would just go with Eau Intense for your spring and summer over your Nautica’s, and even Acqua Di Gio’s. Light Blue especially at discounters is a happy medium price-wise. Right now for about $65 that's a full presentation you can get a 200ml. (If you're at Ulta, Macy's, or Dillard's right now reading this before you decide.) Let me help you out! Get back in your car go home shop at a discounter online. At the price of that 100ml at any of those places you can buy (2) 200ml at a discounter.

If you happen to give this one a smell you might find yourself getting a backup.

Enjoy

baseerelech21 04/11/25 05:15

D&G intended this for warmer weather/summer use. Which is amazing and I think they hit the nail on the head pretty well! I only wished that this scent lasted longer as it has a very pleasant, light, and clean smell! Wish it could last 5+ hours on me... Low-key, can't get enough of it LOL! Will definitely consider repurchasing again!

*PROS:*
- Great for warm weather/summer
- Nice and light scent (clean beachy vibes)
- None overpowering scent profile/projection radius (you and others around you can still comfortably breathe!)
- Smooth transitions between layers
- Better for indoor settings (*PERSONAL*)
- 1 or 2 initial spray(s) is good enough
- Perfect, if you want a scent that doesn't last too long (a few hours max)

*CONS:*
- Bad if you want a scent that lasts long (5+ hours)
- Scent can't shine it's best in an outdoor setting
- After initial application, the projection radius deteriorates WAAAAAY too quickly (after about an hour or so of application: projection radius comes to about arm's length or hugging distance)
- Some reviews said that it lasts long, but I personally don't think it lasted that long (3hrs max, and avg. 2hrs)... (*PERSONAL*)
- Upon first 30 seconds, the scent swiftly explodes outwards to create a projection radius (mine was about a 2 meters), and stays there for about 40 - 60 minutes. Afterwards, the projection radius deteriorates to about half or less of the initial radius, and stays there for about another 40 - 60 minutes. After that, the radius shrinks again to be about arm's length or contact distance (i.e. hugging) for the scent to be detectable, which lasts for about another 40 - 60 minutes. Finally it checks out until only you (the wearer) or someone else puts their nose up against the area of contact that you sprayed on.

Citrus in 90+ degree heat? This stuff laughs at the sun while you melt. Stays close, sticks for 5–6 hours, and actually likes sweat. Yeah, you heard me—sweat and heat are its best friends. If you’re an office zombie sitting in a cubicle all day, grab your Chanel 5 or Sauvage. This? Made for beast mode humans only.

Opening hits like a grapefruit and orange grenade—sweet, tangy, mouth-watering. A few minutes later, sea notes roll in like a salty ocean breeze crashing into your skin, backed by just enough juniper to say, “Yes, I’m fancy, but I don’t care.” Leaves behind a soft, powdery, woodsy trail. Facts.

And for all y’all whining, “Smells like grandpa” or “piss”:
Let me educate you.
You’d be doing good to smell and look like me at my age 🤦♀️.
This old grandpa? Still gettin’ it.
Kids, take notes.

Spray heavy. Sweat. Run around like a maniac.
You cannot overdo it. People will stop and say, “Wow, that smells amazing!”
Nobody.
I repeat.
Nobody is thinking “grandpa” or “piss.”

This is fresh. Clean. Summer beast mode.
Ocean breeze, citrus bomb, salty sea vibes.
Old dude still schooling the kids.
Stay hydrated. Spray responsibly. Flex your nose.

Carlitos 01/18/25 00:57

A WALK ON THE BRIGHT SIDE OF LIFE

I'm not usually a fan of the light aquatic scents out there. So I was not expecting much from Light Blue Pour Homme Eau Intense. D&G did a lot of (expensive) advertising for this family of fragrances. Probably their aim was to convince customers that using this fragrance would make them look like D&G's chiseled model David Gandy. I suppose it made some sense to me. I wanted to buy a fresh perfume for the gym (the mandarin note is a must for me) and decided to blindly buy this light blue flanker. If I was lucky enough to look like a famous male model, so much the better. I can assure you that, despite all the make-up I've applied, I still don't look the least bit like David Gandy. Probably the steel muscles and macho look will come after the second or third bottle. Driving a red Ferrari hasn't worked for me either.
I usually like the non-fresh D&G fragrances. I was disappointed when I offered my wife the regular Light Blue for Women. It was just one scent too weak. So I never paid any attention to either the regular version of Light Blue Pour Homme or its flankers. Surprise! Surprise! This Intense version is really quite intense!... but that's a comment that only applies to a fresh aquatic fragrance, of course. Well, at least it satisfies my simple need for it.
I liked the scent at first sniff. The fresh, salty, bitter opening accord is a bit lively. It has enough bitterness to balance its sweet and cool nature, with just the right amount of grapefruit, mandarin and marine notes to cut through a hot day or a sweaty session at the gym. Projection and longevity are good by my low standards for a fresh fragrance. I also like its approach to a fresh dry down, but with a light ambry and musky accord. It reminds me of a lighter and more sporty version of Acqua Di Gio Profumo. The downside is the recognisable synthetic aura that this fragrance exudes.
With three sprays, the longevity is easily good enough for more than five hours, while the sillage radius is a little more than an arm's length.
My verdict on Light Blue pour Homme Eau Intense | Dolce & Gabbana is as follows:
___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___
- Opening: 7.0 (nice mandarine/grapefruit/marine opening, but a bit synthetic)
- Dry down: 8.0 (nice fresh dry down, with ambry and musky accords that could qualify this perfume as a blue scent)
- Longevity: 7.5 (up to 5 hours on my skin, with 3 initial sprays; I think it's a little above average for an aquatic fresh scent)
- Sillage: 6.5 (sillage peaks at 4 feet; it lasts for 1.5 hours with 3 sprays)
- Versatility: 6.5 (only for hot or very hot weather)
- Usability: 9.0 (very good for the beach, the office in the summer, everyday use in hot weather, outdoor activities and places where you might sweat like the gym)
- Praise: 7.5 (you'll get a few compliments, but only because you smell fresh and clean)
- Exclusivity: 7.5 (I tried the original Light Blue for Men a long time ago and don't remember it well; many reviewers claim the two scents are similar; I find this Intense version to be slightly different from most fresh marine scents I know, but not much. I once mistook it for "Acqua di Giò Profondo" by Giorgio Armani - only the scent, not the bottle)
- Quality: 8.0 (pleasant notes, but a bit synthetic. Kudos for an acceptable performance)
- Presentation: 9.0 (nice flask with frosted glass, nice lettering, simple but effective; the lettering wears off easily)
- Price: 7.0 (€42.50 for 100ml tester)
___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___
Average: 7.59/10.00
between 7 and 8 = above average
between 8 and 9 = recommended
greater than 9 = don't miss;

MY OPINION on Light Blue Pour Homme Eau Intense:
A nice fresh marine scent with an inviting blue dry down and a slightly above average performance for a fresh scent. If it suits either your needs or your fragrance preferences, go ahead and buy it if you think the price is ok. But there really are plenty of other options.
Is it worth buying blind? Absolutely not!

MUSIC: Lou Reed - "Walk On The Wild Side".

So please, don’t judge it before the drydown, or if you’ve only tested it on a paper strip, this applies to any perfume you're testing.

Note: Perfumes should be tested on your skin or clothes, because that’s where you’ll actually apply it, not on a paper strip or in the air. Also, don’t stick your nose right onto the area where you’ve applied the perfume. People aren’t going to grab your arm, neck, or clothes to smell you—they’ll pick up the scent from the air/aura around you. The perfume’s aura is what people will notice. (This is a basic rule for testing any fragrance)

Ok, hear me out. If you are thinking in buying this or already own this fragrance and you are not liking the Calone (supposedly egg note), I'll give you the best way to use It just because I really love this and I want to share it with you.

First of all, this really does not smell like egg or anything like that. In the air this smells just like if you mixed slightly sour citrus, sea notes, salt, a little aromatic and tiny sweet in the middle from the juniper and on the base it is musky and has a reminiscence of woody notes.
This is stands out from all the blue and citrus oriented fragrances because there is an absence of vetiver and patchouli which are pretty common on those type of frags.

Now, the best way to use this is to use it in a really hot weather, over 24°C to be precise. This is due to the fact that lower temperatures just eats the sour citruses note and let that Calone be more sharp. This becomes an unbalanced fragrance on colder weather.

Another important thing is to let the juice touch your skin right out of the shower and use really clean clothes. You still may smell a little of the Calone but if you followed this mini guide you just let pass some 5 to 10 min and it will really shine. This projects and stays on for a really long time.

Furthermore it can smell a bit eggy initially for someone who is not familiar with Alberto Morillas fragrances but take it from someone who wasn't a fan of his creations, it does grow on you and that eggy note disappears leaving you with one of the best summer fragrance of current time.

Tuvok 01/04/20 06:54

Everybody knows Light Blue. It's synthetic, boring, extremely pleasing to women and it sucks at longevity and projection. It is a pleasant refreshment during a hot day but you need to respray every 3 hours because it fades away. With Eau Intense everything changes. The scent I never wanted to buy because of the weak performance, thanks to the intense version, is now in my collection. The longevity with that one is superb on my skin. It's a fresh aquatic-citrusy scent so who would have thought that it's gonna last more than 12 hours on my skin. For 3 hours 2 sprays behind the ears project nicely. It is slightly different than the original Light Blue, especially in the opening, but after some time I can't smell any obvious difference, but I never had a bottle of the original juice. It is still nothing original, it is generic, but when you own some niche scents like me, you know that sometimes you are tired of all that amber, incense and oud and you just want smell fresh at the grocery store or something. Then, that is the right choice guys. Imho it's good for all seasons but it will shine especially during the spring days and summer nights. It is cheap too. Got 100 ml for 40 Euros.
